DELL and ADI earnings today (estimated, time not set): a read on AI server and chip demand
Wed 08:30: GDP second estimate and October PCE inflation, plus Hormuz tanker and oil headlines tonight
market.if_then: If QQQ is back above 641.95 after the first hour, then buy only the strongest names on their triggers below; if it stays under 641.95, then make no new buys and let the gap-down play out.

stocks.headline: Down 5.3% premarket at 156.36, giving back part of Monday's 31.5% jump after Huang was reinstated as CEO.
stocks.why: Monday's jump was relief that the founder is back. Today the market is pricing the cost: analysts now call Huang 'too big to fire', which puts the board's oversight under scrutiny. The US also added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist over fears that advanced chips were being diverted, coming after TSMC and Samsung halted some shipments to China. The business is not the problem: EPS was 2.68 against 2.47 expected, sales grew 106%, forecasts are up 28% in 90 days, and the stock trades at 9.9× forward profit. That makes this a governance and China story, not an earnings one. NVDA leads the whole AI group, so a break here drags MU, TSM, ARM, SMCI, CRWV and AMD with it.

long_term.reason: Growth and margins are the strongest in this group and the stock is at its cheapest in 5 years. But governance and China export risk are new and unresolved, so this is not the day to add.

stocks.what_would_change_it: New export restrictions that reach NVDA's own China sales would cut the stock to Trim; a close back above 165.05 with the governance story calming would make it an Add.
stocks.action: Keep what you own and don't buy the open. Add only if it closes back above 165.05.

levels.means: above = the comeback rally is back on and adding is justified; below = still digesting Monday
above = Monday's gains mostly hold; below = the rally is unwinding, so expect more selling into the afternoon
above = the reinstatement gap still stands; below = the whole relief move has failed, so stop buying the AI group

stocks.if_then: If NVDA trades below 143.73, then cut any trading position opened Monday and keep only the long-term core.

stocks.headline: Down 6.8% premarket at 659.51 after jumping 19.0% Monday, almost all of it with the market.
stocks.why: MU moves about twice as much as the market, so it gives back the most when the AI trade cools. Little of the swing is company news. The business is booming: sales up 345%, a 75% operating margin, 134.0B of contracted backlog and a 3.4× forward P/E. The next real test is earnings on Dec 17. A stock this cheap on numbers this strong is a long-term holding, but in a RED tape its swings are too large to chase.

long_term.reason: Backlog, margins and rising forecasts all support the price; the risk is how volatile it is, not the business.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A sign the memory price cycle is turning, such as forecast cuts ahead of Dec 17, would move it to Trim.
stocks.action: Hold your shares and don't buy the gap-down. Add only if it reclaims 666.66 and holds there into the close.

stocks.headline: At 109.99 premarket (down 3.2%) after a 12.3% jump Monday, still near its 52-week low of 100.25.
stocks.why: ORCL holds 664.0B of contracted backlog, sales growth is speeding up to 30%, and the stock trades at 10.3× forward profit, its cheapest in 5 years. It fell with the AI spending scare, not on its own results. The risk is the cost of building the data centers that backlog requires, and analysts expect EPS to fall 16% in the Dec 14 report, which usually moves the stock about 11%. If the AI group steadies, ORCL has the most room to recover.

long_term.reason: A huge contracted backlog, faster growth and a record-low valuation. The house view is Buy now and nothing overnight changes that.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A Dec 14 report that shows spending outrunning cash, or backlog slipping, would move it to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open. Buy a first piece only if it trades back at or above 112.28, and add the rest after Dec 14.
